input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Section 10(a) gives us a broad Kubient defend-and-indemnify obligation for third-party Claims arising out of or in connection with the Services, the Auction Platform, the Creative, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. Because Kubient's warranties in Section 9(b) expressly include non-infringement of third-party IP (9(b)(i), (vii), (viii)), compliance with applicable Law (9(b)(v), (ix)) and secure handling of data (9(b)(iii)), the indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement claims, breach of law, data security failures and Kubient's own misconduct — meeting the preferred position, with no IP carve-out and no super-cap or aggregate liability cap limiting it (Section 7 preserves indemnification liability from the consequential-damages waiver). Section 11 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a forfeiture, indemnitor control of defence with consent required for liability-admitting settlements, cooperation at the indemnitor's cost). Our reciprocal indemnity in Section 10(b) is confined to our own Content and Properties, our own breaches and our own acts or omissions rather than Kubient's Services; the references to our "unauthorized or inappropriate use" and acts/omissions are marginally wider than the preferred narrow formulation, which we note but do not redline as it does not shift indemnity for the Services onto us.
